findings.text: The AI pattern-and-mood trader is the only listed strategy ahead after costs: 20 trades, 15 wins, net +322.5 USD (+1.61%). Both baselines lost: momentum -446.64 (-0.43%) over 105 trades, always-up -876.78 (-0.48%) over 183. All trading so far is this week; 20 trades prove little, and no luck test is in the inputs.

No rule strategy and none of the other AI traders shows a settled trade in the leaders; the EOD notes say the facts hold no rule-family result. So rule versus AI, and news weight versus no news, are untested. The inputs do not say whether they abstained, missed their threshold or failed a gate; check abstentions first.

The AI leader mostly rode sector swings: its LLY and WMT wins are tagged sector_lift, and its DE win was the same trade always-up also won. Its DAL loss came from market and sector declines, not the company. Fewer trades, not shown stock-specific insight, is the likely gap so far (reasoning only).

Baseline losses repeat the same moves across horizons and both baselines: CAT company-specific misses appear on two horizons, and the same UAL market-driven miss appears in each baseline. Overlapping trades share one price path, so the 183 and 105 trade counts overstate independent evidence.

Verified news gave no evidence either way: every corroborated or confirmed_primary group has 1 event, not enough events yet. The NVDA up call that relied on a corroborated chip-financing headline closed at 217.23 from 237.47. The EOD notes found news explained none of the reviewed moves. Whether verified news helps remains untested.

Rows with enough events are unverified, promotional or single_source, which the model weights little or not at all, and the largest mirror sector moves: sector promotional high news +7.1963% while its sector fell -6.921%; macro unverified medium -3.091% while its sector rose +2.461%. One week of this is no basis for changing news weights.
